title: Cataclysm 0.8 — corrective build: upgrade UI, uncapped progression, paced enemy unlocks
prompt: CORRECTIVE RELEASE for the already playable Cataclysm 0.8. Keep the public name and runtime version EXACTLY 'Cataclysm 0.8'; use a distinct technical build ID/commit for traceability. This is a same-version revision, NOT 0.9 and NOT a cosmetic patch. The tester compared 0.8 against 0.7 and found the upgrade-menu bug persists, upgrade caps still prevent progression, and practically every enemy type is already present by ~3 minutes. Treat these three issues as P0 release blockers. Start with current docs/preview source, preserve existing playable mechanics, studio/dashboard, private video and stable /preview/ URL. Diagnose the actual upgrade overlay on touch-screen portrait: it currently renders up to 14 upgrade buttons inside the arena; investigate viewport clipping, scrolling, overlays, inaccessible choices, disabled options, double clicks, freeze/resume, focus, pointer input, and level-up reentry. Fix ROOT CAUSE, not just styles. Make every offered option visible and tap-able on 360x780 and 390x844; prefer 3 clearly presented upgrade choices per level (with recover as a viable fallback) or an intentionally scrollable/paged and thoroughly tested dialog. After choosing, apply exactly one upgrade and resume gameplay, including consecutive levels in one fish cache; no softlocks. Rework upgrade logic to REMOVE arbitrary gameplay progression caps and total special-pick budget (currently damage 3, speed +108, cooldown 0.24s, multi-shot/ricochet/magnet two ranks, 4 combined specials, companion rank 3, HP 6). Repeated choices should continue to improve the build or transform into explicit meaningful scaling after former limits; no silently disabled familiar options because a hidden budget was exhausted. Use diminishing returns, hit/projectile aggregation, and measured performance protections if truly needed instead of an arbitrary player-facing progression wall. Keep defensive maximum active-enemy/projectile limits as technical safety controls, not as reasons to stop offering gameplay upgrades; update all UI descriptions, diagnostics, and help that still claim capped upgrades. REBALANCE enemy introduction around simulation elapsed time and readable progression; inspect actual variant logic (currently weaver/dasher from level>=3, orbiter night 3, stalker night 5, ghost night 6, gas night 8, night increments every 24 seconds). Do not front-load all classes by 180 seconds. Space major archetypes, hazards, boss encounters and surprises over a substantially longer survival run (target distinct new threats into 10-20+ minute runs); let familiar enemies evolve before each new unlock, and ensure existing enemy archetypes remain attainable eventually. Make pacing robust against early power spikes/fast leveling, preserve a meaningful early game, avoid escalation solely by raw enemy count or speed. Add deterministic tests for sequential unlock timing and long-run availability at 3, 5, 10, 15, 20 minutes, plus repeat level-up, capped-old-build regression and touch overlay interactions. Use independent mobile Chromium QA; include concrete observed timings, before/after caps, tests and any limitations in coder report. NO new game, new studio, extra recording transcription, or unrelated change. Release only if objective acceptance checks pass; do not hide test failures. Technical patch build identifier distinguishes the corrected 0.8 from its first upload.
acceptance: Version shown in title, gameplay, boot handshake and release metadata remains 0.8, not 0.9; new technical build identifier identifies the correction.

Upgrade menu is fully usable at 360x780 and 390x844 portrait via actual touch emulation: all presented choices reachable, tap targets usable and no clipping/scroll lock; regression tests cover failing previous state.
Upgrade freezes simulation, shows real valid choices, applies precisely one choice, restores play input, and handles successive level-ups without stalls or duplicate grants.
No arbitrary player-facing damage, speed, fire-rate, HP, special-pick or companion rank limits terminate progression at the former numeric thresholds; repeat-upgrade tests cross every old cap.
Game still has a safe, performant plan for very high attack/movement values and projectile counts; no runaway memory/CPU from an uncapped build.
No all-enemy-type saturation by simulation minute 3; capture and assert actual variant availability at t=0, 180, 300, 600, 900 and 1200 seconds.
New enemy archetypes and hazards continue to unlock through substantially longer runs, including beyond minute 10, rather than being exhausted within the opening few minutes.
Spawn timing and boss/hazard staging remain predictable under sudden level spikes, with no accidental fast-unlock from player level alone.
All current core combat, fish XP, beacons, familiars, feral instinct, mobile touch, sound/pause/restart, scoreboard and diagnostics continue to function.
Help copy and visible upgrade descriptions accurately reflect reworked rules, with no obsolete cap notices.
Run game-specific progression regressions and independent browser touch tests, document concrete results; reject rather than publish a merely cosmetic or unverified fix.
Publish and verify changed bytes at the same /preview/ URL only after acceptance and QA; preserve prior release commit for rollback.
